english: Friend, I have driven your wagon here. On the path a wheel broke. My wagon! My grandfather built that wheel. I did not want it. I will make you a new wheel. You do not build wheels. Then I will give you two rams. That is a straight word. Drive the rams into my field.

english: Look at the cow that I led home yesterday. That is my cow! At night a thief drove her away from my field. I did not know it; I got her in trade for three sheep. Who sold her to you? A stranger sold her; he had a black horse. He is a thief. Give me my cow, and take two sheep. That is right. May the gods find the thief.

english: Woman, I have silver. What is silver? I do not know it. It is white, and kings love it. Does it give milk? It gives no milk; with it you buy cows. Your silver is cold, and I do not sell my cattle. Then let me get your wool in trade for silver. Wool I will sell you; my daughter wants a beautiful thing.

english: Of-Good-Fame, I am going home. I give you this cup. It is beautiful. Where did you find it? My brother got it in trade for two rams. Do not go away! Take this garment; my wife wove it. Giver of good things, may the gods give you good things. Be well, guest, and come again in spring.

english: Of-True-Fame, I owe you three sheep. Here I lead six lambs to you. Are six lambs better than three sheep? In a year the lambs will be sheep. And who will nourish them in winter? I will give you six loads of grain. Then lead the lambs into my stall. Now you owe me nothing. May the gods guard you and your sheep.

pie: bʰréh₂ter toy h₃rḗǵs bʰl̥Hóm márkom h₁opéyet. kʷód déh₃rom h₁ésmey déh₃esi? déh₃rom moy tósyo déh₃rōd méǵyos h₁éstu. kʷíd h₁éḱwōd méǵyos? kéh₂nmn̥ h₁éḱwōd méǵyos. h₁éḱwos mért kéh₂nmn̥ gʷíh₃woh₂. h₃rēǵéy kéh₂nmn̥ séngʷʰōh₂ tósyo-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti. h₃réǵes h₂éh₂usom lubʰyónti. nu h₁ésmey h₂éh₂usom kéh₂nmn̥-kʷe bʰérōh₂.
english: Brother, the king gave you a white horse. What gift will you give him? Let my gift be greater than his gift. What is greater than a horse? A song is greater than a horse. A horse dies; a song lives. I will sing a song for the king, and his fame will be imperishable. Kings love gold. Then I will bring him gold and a song.

english: Grandmother, my mother gives you this wool. Show it to me, child. The wool is white and soft. What does your mother ask for? She asks for wheat and salt. Take three measures of wheat. I have little salt. Is that price right? It is right. Carry the wheat to your mother.

english: Woman, I carry salt from the marsh. Do you need salt? I need it; our cattle lick salt. What do you ask for? Give me wool and a hide. I will sell wool; I will not sell a hide. Then wool and butter. Sit down, guest, and drink milk. My daughter will carry the wool to you. You are dear to me; may your cattle be fat.

english: Friend, why are you angry? Do you not remember the cow? Last year I drove a cow to you, when your herd died. I remember it, and she brought forth a young one. Then you owe me the cow and the young one? I owe you the cow, and let the young one be yours. Your word is straight. A good man does not forget a gift. In the morning I will drive the two of them to your field.

pie: awis akwāsas ka.
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: tat kukruwants awis agram ā bʰugat.

english: Of-Goodly-Fame, my house is empty, and my children are hungry. Give me grain, I ask you. Will you plough my field in spring? I will plough it, and I will sow your seed. Then take four loads of grain. When the harvest comes, you will receive a share. You are a good man; the gods see you.

english: Mother, what is a bride-price? A bride-price is cattle. The young man's kin give it to the woman's father. What did my father give to your kin? He gave nine cows and a cauldron of bronze. My uncle wanted ten cows. And what will my bride-price be? A hundred horses! You are dear to us. Then let a king come! Let him come, and let him drive his cattle here.

pie: pótey yóh₁r̥ léytt. méne moy misdʰóm dh₃dʰí. h₂ówins moy péh₂s wĺ̥kʷos-kʷe h₂egʷnóm ne h₁épt. kʷóm misdʰóm gʷʰédʰyesi? déḱm̥ h₂ówins wr̥h₁énm̥-kʷe gʷʰédʰyoh₂. tód wésni wéwkes. tód wéwkom memónh₂e-kʷe. déḱm̥ h₂ówins wl̥h₁só. spéh₁istās wl̥h₁h₂é. túH ǵn̥h₃rós poh₂imḗn.
english: Master, the year has gone. Give me my wage. You guarded my sheep, and the wolf seized no lamb. What wage do you ask for? I ask for ten sheep and a ram. You said it in spring. I said it, and I remember. Choose ten sheep for yourself. I choose the fattest ones. You are a wise shepherd!

pie: owis eḱwōskʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: Old man, why are you looking at me? I knew your father. Your father owed my brother a bull. I did not know it. Did he not give it? He died in the winter of the great snow. A son carries his father's load. Then I owe you the bull. You are a true son. Give me a cow's young one, and I will forget the bull. In spring I will lead the best young one to you.

english: Sister, I have much barley, and I have no wool. I have wool, and I need barley. Let me get your wool in trade for my barley. How many loads of barley do you bring? I bring four loads. This wool is heavy. Give six loads. Five loads and a cup of honey. That is right. My children will rejoice.

english: I have a fat pig, and you have a big cauldron. You desire my cauldron? I desire it; my cauldron broke in the fire. Your pig's legs are thin, and its belly is small. It eats grain, and it will be fat. Bring it in winter, when it is fat. And in what shall I cook meat? Take the cauldron now; I trust you.

english: Taste this honey! It is sweet. Where did you find it? I found it in an old tree. Fill this pot with barley. The pot is big, and the honey is little! But honey is sweeter than barley. That is true. I will fill the pot halfway. Fill it, and in spring I will bring you honey again.

english: The winter is long, and we have no grain. Let me exchange my foal for barley. Your foal is young; in three winters he will be a strong horse. Why do you give him away? Hunger is in my house, and we do not eat horses. Then do not give me the foal. Take six measures of barley. In the harvest season give me barley. You are kind; may the gods fill your belly with grain.

HeHḱúm h₁n̥ḱdʰí. kʷíd HeHḱúm gʷr̥néHsi? polh₁éwes h₂egʷnṓs tósmōd ǵn̥h₁yṓntor. nu HeHḱúm wélh₁oh₂er. kʷíh₁ tóm pérh₂esi? kʷetesr̥bʰí h₂éwibʰis sh₂lés-kʷe médesh₁.
english: Tell me. Which ram is better? This one is bigger; that one is swifter. I choose the big one; his wool is thick. The big one is old; in a year he will be weak. Take the swift one. Why do you praise the swift one? Many lambs will be born from him. Then I will choose the swift one. For what will you sell him? For four sheep and a measure of salt.

pie: h₂énHe moy spélom wéwke. ḱléwse. gʷṓws h₂n̥réy h₁ést. gʰóstis tósyo dṓm gʷémt sweh₂dú-kʷe kéh₂nmn̥ gʷéHyet. h₂nḗr kéh₂nmn̥ swóh₁ gʷéwh₁ kʷrinéh₂t. só ǵn̥h₃rós ne h₁ést? tósyo pótnih₂ gʰrémet. só lelóykʷe kéh₂nmn̥-kʷe kh₂nómes. tód moy kh₂né.
english: Grandmother, tell me a story. Listen. A man had a cow. A guest came to his house and sang a sweet song. The man bought the song with his own cow. Was he not wise? His wife was angry. She is gone, and we sing the song. Sing it to me!

english: I killed an aurochs, and I bring you its horn. An aurochs! Were you not afraid of him? I was afraid; my spear pierced his heart. At the feast men will drink mead from that horn. I will give you five measures of wheat. Give eight measures, and the horn shall be yours. Seven measures, and at night drink mead with me. I take seven measures, and I will drink with you.

pie: h₂éwh₂e moy wr̥h₁dʰí. kʷíh₁ ḱóm márkom kʷrinéh₂s? h₂éh₂usoh₁. gʰóstis nos h₁ím ḱóymom ǵʰiméni wédʰet. gʰóstis h₃reǵtós wiHrós h₁ést? só h₃reǵtós ne h₁ést. polh₁ú h₂éh₂usom gʷʰédʰyet dʰréwgʰt-kʷe me. kʷíh₁ te dʰréwgʰt? h₂éǵt só h₂yuHn̥ḱós. só sénos h₁ést. só-ge HeHḱús.
english: Uncle, tell me. For what did you buy this horse? For gold. In winter a stranger brought him to our village. Was the stranger an upright man? He was not upright. He asked for much gold, and he deceived me. How did he deceive you? He said: he is young. He was old. He is swift indeed.

pie: kʷíh₁ déywoǵenh₁es h₁énom márkom kʷréyh₂oh₂? tóm ne pr̥néh₂mi. h₂éwh₂os moy tóm h₂élet tóm-kʷe stérgoh₂. ḱm̥tóm toy h₂ówins dh₃yéh₁m̥. tóm ǵʰéslom h₂éwibʰis ne pr̥néh₂oh₂. túH moy gʰóstis. ḱóymoy moy nékʷti l̥gʰdʰí pṓlHom-kʷe toy h₂éyeri déh₃oh₂. déh₃nom. kʷíd toy bʰérōh₂? h₁yód h₂ew gʷm̥yḗsi kéh₂nmn̥ moy bʰére.
english: Of-Divine-Race, for what can I get that horse in trade? I do not sell him. My grandfather raised him, and I love him. I would give you a hundred sheep. I will not sell him for a thousand sheep. You are my guest. Lie down in my house at night, and in the morning I will give you a foal. A gift! What shall I bring you? When you come again, bring me a song.

pie: bʰoydʰéh₂m n̥smé h₁entér dʰéh₁omes. séh₂lm̥ toy wésni wéǵʰōh₂ túH-kʷe moy h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m dédeh₃esi. kʷóti sh₂lés bʰórons bʰérēsi? déḱm̥ bʰórons pénkʷe márkōys woǵʰéyōh₂. nu déḱm̥ h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂s h₃énHesh₂ h₁opéyōh₂. dyḗws nos ph₂tḗr bʰoydʰéh₂m widétu. h₁yós dʰrugʰyḗti dyḗws tóm gʷʰéntu. tód h₃m̥néh₃mi ne-kʷe te dʰrugʰyṓh₂.
english: Let us put a pledge between us. In spring I will bring you salt, and you will give me wool. How many loads of salt will you bring? I will bring ten loads with five horses. Then I will give ten loads of wool. Let Dyēus the father see our pledge. Whoever deceives, let Dyēus strike him down. I swear it, and I will not deceive you.
